title: Inverse ambiguous maps on infinite groups
summary: Let $G$ be a group. A bijection $f\colon G\to G$ is called inverse ambiguous if $f^{-1}(x)=f(x)^{-1}$ for every $x\in G$. We prove that every infinite group admits an inverse ambiguous function. An inverse ambiguous automorphism can exist only on an abelian group. We classify the finitely generated and divisible abelian groups admitting such automorphisms. If $A\cong\Z^r\oplus T$, where $T$ is finite, then $A$ admits an inverse ambiguous automorphism if and only if $r$ is even and $T$ admits one.
